description: We are a team of students from Yuriy Fedkovych Chernivtsi National University participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. As part of the “Field Shifts: Adapting Farms with NASA Data” challenge, we use NASA Earth observation data to develop practical tools that help farmers adapt to climate change. By combining software development, data analysis, and visualization, we aim to transform complex satellite data into clear, actionable insights for the agricultural sector.
summary: TerraMind is a digital workspace for farmers built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge (Field Shifts: Adapting Farms with NASA Data). Designed with a global-first architecture, TerraMind synthesizes multi-source Earth observation data-including NASA POWER, SMAP, GPM/IMERG,  MODIS/VIIRS and FAO GAEZ-into an intuitive 5-step decision-support web portal. Farmers and agronomists can delineate field boundaries on interactive satellite maps, diagnose localized climate and soil-moisture risks, and generate optimized 5-year crop rotation plans tailored to soil health, yield stability, and market priorities. Beyond agronomic planning, TerraMind bridges the gap between sustainable farming and green finance through an automated Carbon Credit Pre-Auditor (using satellite NDVI time series for digital Measurement, Reporting, and Verification) turning Earth observation into measurable ecological and economic resilience worldwide.
details:
What TerraMind Does
TerraMind is a digital workspace for farmers, 5-year crop rotation planning, and carbon-farming pre-audit web application built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge (Field Shifts: Adapting Farms with NASA Data). Instead of relying on black-box predictions or expensive field sensors, TerraMind combines deterministic agronomic science with planetary-scale Earth observation data from NASA and FAO.

Through an intuitive interface supporting both Dark and Light modes, farmers and agronomists move across a Dashboard and a structured 5-step guided workflow:

My Fields (Boundaries and Soil): Users search any village, city, or region worldwide and delineate their land directly on an interactive geospatial map using Detect Boundary on Map or manual polygon drawing (+ Draw by Points). The platform calculates Registered Parcels and Total Cultivated Area (ha) while allowing users to toggle between High-Res Satellite, Street Map (OSM), NDVI (NASA Vegetation), and NASA MODIS layers.

NASA Climate (Weather and Risks): In the Climate Analysis module, TerraMind fetches location-specific historical and current agroclimatological data via NASA POWER to evaluate temperature trends, solar radiation, precipitation reliability, frost windows, and drought stress indicators.

Crop History (Past Seasons): Farmers log previous crops grown on each parcel so the planning engine can account for residual soil nutrient depletion, root-zone moisture drawdowns, and pest or pathogen carryover.

Rotation Plan (5-Year Simulation): The Rotation Planner generates a scientifically balanced 5-year sowing sequence tailored to local climate constraints, botanical rotation rules, and the farmer's primary business goal (yield and profit maximization, soil regeneration, or feed and forage production).

Farm Summary (Final Sowing Plan and Carbon Pre-Audit): The final module consolidates the 5-year sowing schedule, agronomic justifications, and an automated Carbon Credit Calculation and Pre-Audit report estimating carbon sequestration potential and eligibility for regenerative farming programs.

How It Works – Key Technical and Agronomic Innovations


Global-First Tiered Data Architecture (Core Satellite Datasets and Regional Adapters)
Many existing agricultural tools rely on region-locked datasets, rendering them non-functional across Ukraine, Europe, and developing agricultural regions. TerraMind solves this with a two-tier modular architecture:

Tier 1 - Global Core Engine: Built on three globally consistent datasets: NASA POWER (which natively integrates SMAP soil moisture and GPM precipitation parameters alongside meteorological data), MODIS NDVI, and FAO GAEZ. Every parcel on Earth—whether in Chernivtsi Oblast, Ukraine, or the American Midwest—receives standardized climate, soil moisture, vegetation, and crop-suitability analysis without geographic blind spots.

Tier 2 - Modular Regional Adapters: The system architecture is designed to connect high-resolution national soil and cadastral databases (such as national land registries in the EU and Ukraine) as plug-in extensions without altering the core simulation logic.

Rule-Based Multi-Factor 5-Year Crop Rotation Engine
Rather than offering generic single-season advice, TerraMind executes a transparent, rule-based agronomic simulation grounded in FAO GAEZ agro-ecological suitability indices (SI) and multi-year satellite telemetry:

Thermal and Moisture Matching: Cross-references crop vegetative duration and frost sensitivity against NASA POWER temperature, solar radiation, and integrated SMAP surface soil moisture profiles to favor drought-resilient crops during water-deficit cycles.

Erosion and Runoff Protection: Uses NASA POWER integrated GPM precipitation intensity data to schedule autumn and winter cover crops that anchor topsoil and prevent wind and water erosion between cash-crop harvests.

Botanical and Economic Optimization: Enforces strict botanical family break intervals to interrupt pest and disease cycles, balances nitrogen-fixing legumes with high-demand cereals and oilseeds, and ranks rotation options according to expected yield norms, forage value, and farmer priorities.

Automated Carbon Credit Calculator and dMRV Pre-Auditor
Small and mid-sized farms frequently miss out on voluntary carbon markets due to high consulting fees and complex verification requirements. TerraMind integrates a built-in Carbon Credit Calculator and digital Measurement, Reporting, and Verification (dMRV) pre-auditor:

Quantifies projected soil organic carbon (SOC) gains and CO2 sequestration resulting from regenerative rotation shifts (introducing cover crops, legumes, and continuous root cover).

Leverages historical and ongoing MODIS NDVI time series to remotely verify vegetation cover and reduced bare-soil periods.

Outputs a structured pre-audit dossier aligned with international regenerative agriculture standards, lowering entry barriers and audit preparation costs for farmers.

Representative Field Case Study

To validate TerraMind’s workflow, we modeled a multi-year transition on arable farmland in Novi Broskivtsi, Chernivtsi Oblast, Ukraine:

Step 1 - Parcel Mapping (My Fields): The parcel is outlined on the interactive High-Res Satellite and NDVI (NASA Vegetation) map layers to establish exact hectare boundaries.

Step 2 - Climate and Risk Diagnostics (NASA Climate): NASA POWER profiles (incorporating SMAP soil moisture and GPM precipitation metrics) reveal late-summer soil moisture deficits paired with intense seasonal rainfall events—highlighting high erosion and yield-volatility risks under bare-fallow practices.

Step 3 - Baseline Input (Crop History): Logging a conventional short-cycle cereal and oilseed history flags elevated nitrogen depletion and pathogen carryover.

Steps 4 and 5 - 5-Year Simulation and Carbon Pre-Audit (Rotation Plan and Farm Summary): TerraMind generates a diversified 5-year rotation integrating nitrogen-fixing legumes, deep-rooted break crops, and winter cover crops timed to local frost-free windows. The Farm Summary delivers a season-by-season sowing plan alongside calculated carbon-credit estimates verified by MODIS NDVI baselines, positioning the farm for carbon-farming onboarding.

Benefits, Sustainability and Global Alignment

Accessible Precision Agronomy: Replaces costly IoT field stations and manual spreadsheet guesswork with free, open-access NASA and FAO Earth observations.

Transparent, Explainable Decisions: Every rotation recommendation is backed by explicit agronomic rules, FAO GAEZ suitability scores, and measurable NASA POWER and MODIS NDVI indicators that agronomists can audit and trust.

Alignment with UN Sustainable Development Goals: Directly supports SDG 2 (Zero Hunger and Sustainable Agriculture) by preserving soil fertility and stabilizing yields, SDG 13 (Climate Action) through verifiable soil carbon sequestration, and SDG 15 (Life on Land) by curbing land degradation and promoting crop diversity.

Business Model and Dual-Track Monetization Strategy


Rather than locking farmers behind rigid paywalls from day one, TerraMind is designed around a flexible scaling architecture that allows the platform to evolve along two distinct monetization pathways:
Track A - Open Farmer Access & Ethical Research Partnerships: Core agronomic planning and satellite diagnostics remain completely free for farmers to maximize grassroots adoption and regional land coverage. Under strict, transparent, and ethical data-governance consent, aggregated and anonymized field insights power collaborations with agricultural think tanks and research institutions. Within this ecosystem, TerraMind connects participating farms directly to international scientific grant programs—such as European research initiatives on niche industrial and bio-based crops (e.g., Taraxacum kok-saghyz / rubber dandelion cultivation under Horizon Europe frameworks). Farmers gain access to funded pilot programs and new crop markets, while TerraMind generates revenue through institutional R&D partnerships and grant consortia.
Track B - Direct Commercial SaaS & High-Value Add-On Services: A dedicated commercial pivot focused on profit maximization through tiered subscriptions and specialized, high-margin services for commercial farms and agri-holdings. This track unlocks advanced capabilities including custom national cadastre connectors, end-to-end dMRV carbon registry onboarding, bespoke yield-risk analytics for financial institutions, and tailored multi-parcel management tools.


Technical Roadmap

Tier-2 Regional Soil and Cadastre Connectors: Adding plug-in adapters for national soil surveys and land registries across the EU, Ukraine, and North America.

Expanded Global Crop and Cover-Crop Library: Extending vegetative duration, nutrient balance, and carbon sequestration coefficients to cover specialty regional crops worldwide.

Direct Carbon Registry Export: Generating standardized JSON and PDF dMRV packages formatted for one-click submission to voluntary carbon platforms.

NASA and Space Agency Partner Data

NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources): Global agroclimatology, solar radiation, temperature, humidity, frost-window datasets, as well as integrated SMAP (surface soil moisture) and GPM (precipitation) parameters.

NASA MODIS NDVI (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer): Global Normalized Difference Vegetation Index time series and map layers for plant-vigor tracking, vegetation stress detection, and cover-crop dMRV verification.

FAO GAEZ (Global Agro-Ecological Zones): Global agro-climatic crop suitability layers (SI), soil constraints, and baseline yield potentials.
